chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The young female sheep (na'jah), if it is fat, is superior to the castrated male sheep (khasi) from the sheep. And he said: The fat ram is better than the castrated male and than the female. And I asked him about the castrated male and about the female, so he said: The female is more beloved to me than the castrated male.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And know that in the sacrificial animals (udhiyah) from camels, only the thmani (two-year-old) is permissible, and it is the one that has completed five years and entered the sixth. And from cows and goats, only the thmani is permissible, and it is the one that has completed one year and entered the second. And from sheep, the jadha' (young sheep of one year) suffices for one year.

key_terms.الثَّنِيُّ: Two-year-old animal (specifically camel or cow in this context)

ai.seo_question: What are the age and gender requirements for valid sacrificial animals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a hierarchy of preference for sacrificial animals, favoring robust, fat specimens and specifically preferring the female sheep over the castrated male, reflecting the Shia emphasis on selecting the best quality (khayr) for worship. Shaykh al-Tusi’s appended commentary provides the essential fiqh criteria for age and maturity, distinguishing between the five-year-old camel, the two-year-old cow, and the one-year-old goat, while noting that a six-month-old lamb (jadha') suffices for sheep, thereby bridging the Prophetic tradition with practical juristic application.
